text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crisis over relocation of local council headquarters escalates as three people are feared dead in riot that has closed flow stations of Shell oil company.
- Fuel scarcity eases as petrol is discharged at Lagos port. More deliveries expected on Friday.
- State oil company NNPC closes London office because of cash crunch.

- Italian utility power firm ENEL is seeking the assistance of another Italian conglomerate ENI to dispose of 3.5 billion cubic metres of liquefied natural gas it is contracted to buy from Nigeria from 1999.
- Nigerian human rights commission says draconian decrees will be reviewed.

- Chamber of commerce to refund 1.25 billion naira spent by petroleum trust fund, a government agency, to rehabilitate a facility in the north where an African trade fair is to be staged from Saturday.

- Ecobank Nigeria Plc raises capital base to 534 million naira from 133.5 million naira following government directive that banks should recapitalise to a minimum level of 500 million naira by end of 1998 from 50 million naira currently.
- Despite European Union (EU) sanctions on Nigeria, the nation is to attend meeting of African, Carribean and Pacific states with the EU next month in The Netherlands.
- About 390,000 barrels per day of crude oil is feared to be at risk because of protests in the midwestern town of Warri over relocation of a local government headquarters.
